_comment: Where server cores come from. Addresses are data on purpose: they belong to
other people, they move, and a moved address should cost a catalogue update
rather than a release of the mod. The shape of each API is code — see the
provider classes — because the three of them do not agree on anything but
'allowed' is the list of hosts this mod may reach at all, redirects included.
Adding a core means adding its hosts here too, and nothing else can be
Paper's api.papermc.io/v2 is retired and answers 410 to everything. It is
not listed here on purpose: the replacement changed the shape of every
answer as well as the address, so this entry and PaperCore move together.
We never host a jar ourselves: the download comes from whoever publishes it.
Re-hosting Mojang's server is against their agreement, and re-hosting anybody
else's is how a mod ends up shipping a version its author has withdrawn.
_sources: Where plugins and mods can be looked for. Data, so that a new one is a
catalogue update — but only where the shape of its API is already known to
the code: see Modrinth and CurseForge beside Catalogue.
CurseForge is marked as needing a key, and there is no key in this file or
anywhere else in the mod. Their terms allow an application to use the API
with a key issued to whoever runs it; one key shipped to everybody is one
account's quota and one account's name on the whole world's requests, and
it gets revoked. So the flag means 'ask the person for theirs', and until
they give one this source is listed, chooseable, and refuses to search.
The colours are the sites' own, so that the button reads as the place it
goes to rather than as another blue word.
'kinds' is which shelves a site actually stocks. CurseForge has a Bukkit
plugins section in its numbering, but it was left behind years ago — plugin
authors publish on SpigotMC, Hangar and Modrinth. Listing it here would mean
offering a shop with nothing on that shelf, and an empty answer reads as
'there is nothing like that' rather than 'you are asking in the wrong shop'.
_pictures: Hosts pictures inside a description may be fetched from, on top of 'allowed'.
Two lists rather than one because the two risks are not the same size. A jar
is code and is run; a picture is bytes that go through a decoder and are
drawn. So the list a jar may come from stays as short as it can be, and this
one may hold the places mod authors actually put their screenshots.
It is still a list. A description is written by a stranger, and fetching
whatever address it names would hand this player's address to whoever wrote
it — a picture is the oldest way there is to do that. Anything not here is
shown as a line naming the host, with a button that opens it in a browser,
where the person has already decided to go.
